items.quote: came to Jehoiada the priest. Then he gave the commanders the spears and shields
items.contrast: The giver, Jehoiada, versus the weapons’ former owner, King David.
items.reason: King David is a plausible distraction because the weapons had belonged to him. However, “he” refers to the just-mentioned Jehoiada, while David is identified only as their former owner. The question and key correctly resolve giver versus owner.

items.quote: So the man of God interceded with the Lord
items.contrast: The man of God who prays versus the king who requests the prayer.
items.reason: The king is a plausible alternative because he asks for help and is the beneficiary. The next sentence explicitly makes the man of God the one who intercedes, so the key uniquely identifies the praying agent.

items.quote: the city was calm, because Athaliah had been slain with the sword at the palace.
items.contrast: Athaliah’s death as the stated cause versus the people’s rejoicing as a simultaneous result.
items.reason: The people’s rejoicing is a plausible alternative because it appears beside the city’s calmness. However, the explicit “because” clause gives Athaliah’s death as the cause, so the key is uniquely supported.

items.quote: And since their land lacked nothing, they were prosperous.
items.contrast: The land’s lack of nothing as the cause of prosperity versus similarity to the Sidonians as a description of safety.
items.reason: Living like the Sidonians is a plausible distraction because it is another description of conditions in Laish. The passage explicitly links prosperity to the land lacking nothing with “since,” uniquely supporting the key.

items.quote: I solemnly consecrate my silver to the Lord for my son to make an image overlaid with silver.
items.contrast: The son named in the mother’s statement versus the silversmith who later actually makes the idol.
items.reason: The silversmith is a strong alternative because the later narration says he makes the idol. However, the question specifically asks what the mother says, and her quoted statement names her son. The key uniquely resolves reported intention versus later action.
